en.title: Count Balance After Deleting Digit-Specified Numbers of Parentheses
en.description:
The string contains only left parentheses `(`, right parentheses `)`, and digit characters. Process it from left to right; each time you meet a digit d, you may delete any d of the not-yet-deleted parentheses to its left. Digits are processed one character at a time; for example, `11` means processing 1 and then 1 again. After processing, the string is balanced as long as the number of remaining left parentheses equals the number of remaining right parentheses; no prefix is required to be a valid parenthesis sequence.

**Note:** The upstream example wrongly lists `())` as balanced; its counts are unequal, so the correct result is 0.

Added by this site: standard input is a single-line string of length 1..200000 containing only `(`, `)`, `0`..`9`; if a digit exceeds the number of parentheses not yet deleted before it, all remaining parentheses are deleted. The original problem gives no length range or input/output protocol.
en.input:
A single line containing the string s.

en.output: Output 1 if some valid choice of deletions leaves equal numbers of left and right parentheses, otherwise output 0.
en.explanation: See the endpoint dynamic programming proof in the accompanying notes for details.
hints: After the same prefix is processed, the total number of remaining parentheses does not depend on the deletion choices.
For the same remaining total, the reachable differences between the left and right counts form a contiguous range of the same parity.
Each digit only needs to update the two endpoints of the difference range.
